messages:
maya: quick check — I'm planning to bump replicas on inference-sts from 3 -> 5 to handle higher QPS. worried about PDB + HPA interactions and our preStop drain (30s) making the rollout stall. any objections?
ash: +1 on bump for capacity. main risk is PDB.minAvailable vs HPA.scalingDown, can cause eviction to be blocked. do we need minAvailable=1 or something looser? :thinking: 
sam: what's the current terminationGracePeriod and preStop script doing? if preStop holds connections for 30s that adds to termination time. might starve the canary window.
maya: TGP has terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60, preStop sleeps 30s while we flush connections to local gRPC sidecar. wanted to avoid dropping inflight kv cache.
jorge: if we reduce preStop to 10s and keep terminationGracePeriod at 60 we still have cushion for sidecars to exit gracefully. also suggest adding `maxUnavailable: 1` to rollingUpdate so we don't drop more than one at once.
ash: note: for StatefulSet rollingUpdate `partition` behavior + PDB is tricky. We're using a Deployment-like StatefulSet for ordinal placement. maybe prefer `RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable: 1` on the associated controller?
maya: infra change plan (terraform) — planning to change k8s_stateful_set.replicas = 5 and add annotation for rollout: `redwood.com/rollout-safety: "maxUnavailable=1"` — quick look? here's the TF snippet:
```
resource "kubernetes_stateful_set" "inference" {
  metadata {
    name = "inference-sts"
    annotations = {
      "redwood.com/rollout-safety" = "maxUnavailable=1"
    }
  }
  spec {
    replicas = 5
    update_strategy {
      type = "RollingUpdate"
    }
    template { /* trimmed */ }
  }
}
```
ash: tiny nit — annotations don't change controller behavior; you need the field in spec.update_strategy. for k8s <1.25 statefulset.RollingUpdate doesn't accept maxUnavailable, that's for Deployments. we can emulate by adding a pre-check job that scales up ordinal 4->5 first, then sets partition afterwards. messy.
sam: alternatively we can: 1) scale replicas to 4 first, wait for stable; 2) bump to 5. avoids PDB contention and keeps slow drain safe. doable as two-step TF apply.
maya: ok i'm leaning two-step apply. can we also tweak preStop to 10s in same first apply? that would help.
jorge: +1. update the preStop script to flush only active connections; if it's blocking on cache writes consider async flush on termination.
ci-bot: terraform plan finished — shows `~ kubernetes_stateful_set.inference.replicas: 3 -> 5` and `~ kubernetes_stateful_set.inference.template.spec.containers[0].lifecycle.preStop.exec` changed (30s -> 10s). plan: ~2 to apply.
maya: thanks. i'll split into two applies: (1) change preStop to 10s + replicas=4, apply; (2) after infra stability, replicas=5 apply.
ash: ping me when you do first apply, i'll watch PodDisruptionBudget and HPA scaling events. :eyes: 
ci-bot: canary deploy job queued — will roll 1 new pod at a time for canary labels (test-canary=true).
maya: scheduled first apply in 15m. tagging @ash @sam @jorge for visibility.
jorge: if anything odd, run `kubectl get sts inference-sts -o yaml` and `kubectl describe pdb inference-pdb` — that usually shows the blocker.
ash: also tail the HPA events: `kubectl get hpa inference-hpa -w` — it will show scale decisions.
sam: please also note grafana alert `inference.pod_eviction_blocked` will fire if PDB blocks.
maya: great — thanks team. will report back after first apply. :thumbsup:
